subject: The Fells Fairies" Book Discussion
overview: Author Wendy Pfaffenbach discussed her children's book "The Fells Fairies," which addresses environmental conservation of the Middlesex Fells. The interview covered the book's local inspirations, the author's writing process, and upcoming sequels.

items.title: Introduction of Guest
items.summary: Host Danielle Balocca introduced Medford resident Wendy Pfaffenbach, a geography teacher and author.

items.title: Local Dining Recommendations
items.summary: Pfaffenbach identified Meat Cheese Pizza in West Medford as her favorite local restaurant.

items.title: Discussion of "The Fells Fairy"
items.summary: The author described her book as a story about two girls, based on her own daughters, who work with the Queen of the Fairies to protect the Middlesex Fells from developers.

items.title: Environmental Themes and Local Inspiration
items.summary: Pfaffenbach explained that the plot was inspired by a past hospital development controversy on the Melrose line and serves as a commentary on the misuse of "green" branding.

items.title: Youth Advocacy and Character Backgrounds
items.summary: The discussion highlighted the importance of young people finding their voices and using real-life family anecdotes, such as selling Girl Scout cookies, to build scenes.

items.title: Writing Process and Challenges
items.summary: Pfaffenbach shared her strategy of waking up early to write before her teaching job and offered advice on overcoming creative blocks through character exercises.

items.title: Sequel and Book Availability
items.summary: The author revealed she is working on a sequel about managing competing stakeholders in the Fells and noted the first book is available at Bookends in Winchester.
